object.name: evi.randlfo~
object.digest: Phase synchronous discontinuity-free random LFO waves with FM and morphing capabilities
object.description: An indulgent (but simple) random LFO modulation source. The main LFO output is slightly curved, and all random wave shapes are phase synchronous and share the same random number generator, so that LFO types can be switched in real time without discontinuities. Various modulation and warping attributes control and shape the output in a smoothly updating manner so that the modulation source can be 'performed'. Various additional data outlets provide synchronous downstream processing options.

inlets.description: Base frequency of internal LFOs, in Hz 0..40

outlets.description: An auxilliary LFO based on the same random distributions and affected by the same controls as the main LFO, but with it's own single shape. Only active if the @aux attribute is on.
White noise sync used in the random distribution
Internal Phasor sync, pre or post warping effect via the @phaseout attribute
Synchronous hard steps used in the random algorithm
Internal phasor sync signal for downstream synchronous processing

messages.name: history
messages.digest: Top level gen~ [history] / History() declarations can be reset by messages to the object

attributes.name: aux
attributes.description: If on, auxilliary LFO is available at outlet 2, if off (default), aux LFO is off and so is the CPU required to process it

attributes.name: depth
attributes.description: The final linear output amplitude 0..1 of both LFOs, negative values also available for inversion

attributes.name: mod
attributes.description: Hz amount to frequency modulate the base LFOs frequency (set at inlet 1), this expands and contracts the main phase ramp time segments, modulating the resulting LFOs in a time-slice contraction and expansion. If 0, modulation is (CPU) off.

attributes.name: offset
attributes.description: The final linear output offset -1..1 of both LFOs. LFOs clip at bipolar boundaries.

attributes.name: phaseout
attributes.description: Select whether or not the 4th phasor outlet is sent out pre-warp or post-warp. Warping exponentially shapes the phasor, so if this attribute is off, the phasor outlet will be linear only (but always post modulation (@mod) effect).

attributes.name: resetauto
attributes.description: If on (the default) phase will be automatically and smoothly reset (to 0) whenever the sum of inlet 1 (main frequency) and @mod attribute is 0 Hz. When Hz is again greater than 0, the LFOs will smoothly ramp up.

attributes.name: skew
attributes.description: Logarithmic shaping of LFO shapes. At extremes, the LFOs will 'hug' one of the bipolar boundaries, as well as favour concave or convex shaping.

attributes.name: warp
attributes.description: Exponentially shape the main internal phasor so that with positive values the phasor slope is concave and with negative values the phasor slope is convex. The overall timing of each phasor ramp remains identical to if it were linear, but this has the effect of squashing or expanding the LFO interpolators around the random value points. It is a cool shaping effect.

attributes.name: wave
attributes.description: Select the LFO wave shape for the main LFO outlet (outlet 1). 0=binary LFO, 1=stepped LFO, 2=linear segments LFO (the default), 3=curved segments LFO. Notes that all waves are phase synchronous and share the same random number generator, as well as set up to avoid hard discontinuities, which means the wave can be switched in real time in a performance oriented way.

attributes.name: zero
attributes.description: Select whether the main internal phase is zero-reset (1) or free running (0, the default). If zero-reset is on, phase frequency only gets updated on phase synchronous boundaries (like MSP [phasor~ @syncupdate 1]). This can have a smooth effect if gradually changing input Hz continuously at higher frequencies, however this may be undesirable if using exclusively low frequency input as the phasor could get stuck at long time intervals. Note that if the @mod attribute is greater than 0, @zero is automatically disabled anyway.
